title: Wall Street ends lower as chip stocks give up gains
summary:
STORY: U.S. stocks ended lower on Thursday, with the Dow dropping nearly two-thirds of a percent, the S&P 500 shedding more than one-third of a percent and the Nasdaq dipping marginally.

Uncertainty around peace talks between the U.S. and Iran weighed on the market, with Iran reviewing a proposal that would stop fighting but leave the most contentious issues unresolved.

Meanwhile, market-leading chip stocks retreated after their recent rally.

:: Arm Holdings

   Archive

U.S.-listed shares of Arm Holdings tumbled 10% as worries about the company's ability to secure sufficient supplies for its new AI chip overshadowed a strong earnings forecast.

Intel and Advanced Micro Devices also declined, giving back some of their gains from earlier this week.

Keith Buchanan, senior portfolio manager at Globalt Investments, said he'd now like to see a broadening of market gains beyond chip makers and other AI-linked companies.

"Leadership has become narrow again. And that's something that concerns us from our framework, is we don't feel like a participation has been what it needs to be to continue to power this bull market forward beyond the point where we are now. So earnings season is really important. We're right in the middle of it right now. So that will give us a little more clarity as to the storylines and, frankly, the momentum that we feel like has to start to spread away from where it's been concentrated over the past week and a half."

:: CoreWeave

Other stock moves on Thursday included cloud provider CoreWeave, which closed down more than 6% but gained in extended trading after beating analysts' estimates for quarterly revenue. The company reported strong demand for its high-performance computing services used to train and deploy AI models.

Shares of Datadog soared 31% after the cloud-monitoring company raised its full-year earnings forecast. Cybersecurity companies CrowdStrike jumped 8% and Palo Alto Networks added 7%.

Elsewhere in the market, shares of Whirlpool slumped nearly 12% after the home-appliance maker missed first-quarter sales estimates and suspended its dividend.

Investors now turn their attention to Friday's nonfarm payrolls report, which is expected to show continued labor market resilience.

title: Wall Street ends lower as chip stocks give up gains
summary:
STORY: U.S. stocks ended lower on Thursday, with the Dow dropping nearly two-thirds of a percent, the S&P 500 shedding more than one-third of a percent and the Nasdaq dipping marginally.

Uncertainty around peace talks between the U.S. and Iran weighed on the market, with Iran reviewing a proposal that would stop fighting but leave the most contentious issues unresolved.

Meanwhile, market-leading chip stocks retreated after their recent rally.

:: Arm Holdings

   Archive

U.S.-listed shares of Arm Holdings tumbled 10% as worries about the company's ability to secure sufficient supplies for its new AI chip overshadowed a strong earnings forecast.

Intel and Advanced Micro Devices also declined, giving back some of their gains from earlier this week.

Keith Buchanan, senior portfolio manager at Globalt Investments, said he'd now like to see a broadening of market gains beyond chip makers and other AI-linked companies.

"Leadership has become narrow again. And that's something that concerns us from our framework, is we don't feel like a participation has been what it needs to be to continue to power this bull market forward beyond the point where we are now. So earnings season is really important. We're right in the middle of it right now. So that will give us a little more clarity as to the storylines and, frankly, the momentum that we feel like has to start to spread away from where it's been concentrated over the past week and a half."

:: CoreWeave

Other stock moves on Thursday included cloud provider CoreWeave, which closed down more than 6% but gained in extended trading after beating analysts' estimates for quarterly revenue. The company reported strong demand for its high-performance computing services used to train and deploy AI models.

Shares of Datadog soared 31% after the cloud-monitoring company raised its full-year earnings forecast. Cybersecurity companies CrowdStrike jumped 8% and Palo Alto Networks added 7%.

Elsewhere in the market, shares of Whirlpool slumped nearly 12% after the home-appliance maker missed first-quarter sales estimates and suspended its dividend.

Investors now turn their attention to Friday's nonfarm payrolls report, which is expected to show continued labor market resilience.

Intel and Advanced Micro Devices also declined, giving back some of their gains from earlier this week.

"Leadership has become narrow again. Investors now turn their attention to Friday's nonfarm payrolls report, which is expected to show continued labor market resilience.

summary: A relative lull in hostilities in the Strait of Hormuz continued early on Sunday as Iran said it was considering a U.S. proposal to end the fighting and reopen the strategic waterway whose closure has cut off a fifth of the world’s oil supply. title: Saudi Aramco Profit Jumps Despite War Disrupting Shipping Routes
summary: Saudi Arabia’s national oil company said its quarterly profit rose 25% as it increased exports via a pipeline that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, after war in the Middle East disrupted shipping through the vital waterway.  Saudi Arabian Oil Co., which is known as Aramco and is the world’s top oil exporter, posted a net profit of $32.5 billion for the three months ending March 31, up from $26 billion in the same period last year.  Oil prices have soared since Iran effectively closed Hormuz after the start of the war with the U.S. and its allies in the region on Feb. 28.

title: Oil prices jump as Trump rejects Iran's response to US peace plan
summary:
STORY: Oil prices rallied Monday, a day after President Donald Trump said Iran's response to a U.S. peace proposal was "unacceptable."

By early afternoon in Asia, international benchmark Brent crude futures were up around 4% at $105 a barrel, with U.S. oil seeing similar gains. 

That reversed declines seen last week, when prices had fallen on hopes of a peace agreement. 

On Monday, the signs of a fraying ceasefire raised supply fears as the Strait of Hormuz stayed largely closed.

It's normally the route for around a fifth of global oil and gas shipments. 

Iran on Sunday released a response to the proposal focused on ending the war.

According to Iranian state TV, Tehran also included a demand for compensation for war damages and emphasized its sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz.

Analysts say the market's attention now shifts to Trump's visit to China.

The president is scheduled to arrive in Beijing on Wednesday and U.S. officials say he's expected to discuss Iran and other topics with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

title: Oil prices jump as Trump rejects Iran's response to US peace plan
summary:
STORY: Oil prices rallied Monday, a day after President Donald Trump said Iran's response to a U.S. peace proposal was "unacceptable."

By early afternoon in Asia, international benchmark Brent crude futures were up around 4% at $105 a barrel, with U.S. oil seeing similar gains. 

That reversed declines seen last week, when prices had fallen on hopes of a peace agreement. 

On Monday, the signs of a fraying ceasefire raised supply fears as the Strait of Hormuz stayed largely closed.

It's normally the route for around a fifth of global oil and gas shipments. 

Iran on Sunday released a response to the proposal focused on ending the war.

According to Iranian state TV, Tehran also included a demand for compensation for war damages and emphasized its sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz.

Analysts say the market's attention now shifts to Trump's visit to China.

The president is scheduled to arrive in Beijing on Wednesday and U.S. officials say he's expected to discuss Iran and other topics with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

summary: Ariana Resources PLC (AIM:AAU, ASX:AA2, FRA:4A6) has confirmed that gold mineralisation at its Dokwe project in Zimbabwe extends at least 150 metres beyond the current resource envelope, with all assays now received from the latest drilling campaign. A JORC resource update is planned for the second half of 2026. Amigo Resources PLC (LSE:AMGO, FRA:0VG) has secured two processing licences in Tanzania, giving it the regulatory green light to advance modular mineral processing hubs at Kabete Mines and Mojimoto. The next phase includes metallurgical test work, drilling and progressive integration of artisanal feedstock into a centralised processing model. Future PLC (LSE:FUTR) has held its full-year guidance despite an 8% drop in first-half revenue, pointing to improving trends across all three divisions in the second quarter. The specialist media group still expects a mid to low single-digit organic revenue decline for the full year with EBITDA margins of 25% to 27%. ACG Metals Ltd (LSE:ACG, OTC:ACGAF) has made its shares eligible for electronic clearing through the Depository Trust Company in the US, making it easier for American investors to access and trade the stock. The shares will continue to settle through CREST in the UK as well. Quantum Blockchain Technologies PLC (AIM:QBT, FRA:BYA1) has extended the maturity of its remaining €2.873 million zero-coupon bond by two years to December 2028. title: Ariana Resources, CelLBxHealth, Tooru, Sintana Energy, 88 Energy, Powerhouse Energy
summary: Ariana Resources PLC (AIM:AAU, ASX:AA2, FRA:4A6) has raised US$19.5 million by selling a 13.6% stake in Turkish gold producer Zenit to fund its Dokwe gold project in Zimbabwe. The company retains a 9.9% interest in Zenit, worth an implied US$14.2 million, along with board representation and dividend rights. CelLBxHealth PLC (AIM:CLBX, FRA:DWV) has secured a collaboration with AdventHealth, one of the largest hospital networks in the US, to deploy its cancer diagnostic platform in two clinical studies. The trials will use CelLBxHealth's technology to track how tumours respond to treatment through simple blood draws rather than invasive biopsies. Tooru PLC (AIM:TOO, FRA:73N) says its portfolio of free-from food brands generated average monthly gross revenue of around £1 million and EBITDA of £150,000 in the first quarter, with both expected to grow through the year. OAF has launched with Asda ahead of expectations, while Pulsin has returned to growth with improved margins. Sintana Energy Inc (TSX-V:SEI, OTCQB:SEUSF, FRA:3ZX1, AIM:SEI) has raised US$11.5 million to fund drilling on the Chevron-operated Nabba-1 well in Namibia, with directors investing US$250,000 each. The oversubscribed raise will also fund acquisitions covering new licence interests in Namibia and Angola. 88 Energy Ltd (AIM:88E, ASX:88E, OTCQB:EEENF, FRA:POQ) has upgraded total gross unrisked resources at its South Prudhoe project in Alaska by 35% to nearly 769 million barrels. The Augusta-1 well is now targeting up to 133.7 million barrels gross, with drilling planned for the 2027 Alaskan winter season. Powerhouse Energy Group PLC (AIM:PHE, FRA:BT81) has won the Energy From Waste Innovation Achievement of the Year at the letsrecycle.com Awards for Excellence 2026. CEO Paul Emmitt called it "a truly proud moment" and "a powerful endorsement of what we have built." Follow us and subscribe on YouTube, our social channels, and on proactiveinvestors.co.uk.

title: Thor Explorations, IXICO, EMV Capital, Empire Metals, Coiled Therapeutics - Small Cap Snapshot
summary: Thor Explorations Ltd (TSX-V:THX, AIM:THX, OTC:THXPF, FRA:T2X) delivered a strong first quarter, with revenue up to $74.3 million and net income rising to $46.7 million as a gold price of $4,820 per ounce more than offset lower sales volumes. The company is on track for 75,000 to 85,000 ounces of production this year and is advancing toward a final investment decision at its Douta project in Senegal. IXICO PLC (LSE:IXI, OTC:PHYOF, FRA:PYPB) is guiding for at least 15% revenue growth this year after a strong first half, with revenue up 23% and its order book growing 38% to £18.1 million. A £10 million fundraise will accelerate the company's TechBio strategy, including a partnership with Medidata, whose platform is used in 80% of FDA novel drug approvals. EMV Capital (AIM:EMVC, FRA:NTK1) grew assets under management 14% to £112.5 million in 2025, with group losses falling 83% to £0.6 million as revenue rose 17%. CEO Dr Ilian Iliev says the group is increasingly optimistic as portfolio companies approach key commercial and regulatory milestones. Empire Metals Ltd (AIM:EEE, OTCQX:EPMLF) has signed a definitive agreement to sell its 75% stake in a non-core gold asset near Kalgoorlie for A$750,000, freeing up capital and management focus for the Pitfield Titanium Project. Pitfield has a mineral resource of 2.2 billion tonnes grading 5.1% TiO₂, making it one of the largest titanium discoveries globally. Coiled Therapeutics (AIM:COIL) has begun trading on the US OTCQB market under the ticker COTXF, giving American investors dollar-denominated access to the oncology company's shares. CEO Sridhar Vempati says 2026 will be "a transformational year," with recent clinical data from its ongoing trial showing an 80% clinical benefit rate.
